Brāhmī is more than two thousand years old and can be learnt to a basic level in a single session. Participants learn the letters, write their own names, and read a few words from an Aśokan edict.

All materials are provided. The session is adapted to your space, your timetable and the age of the participants.

What it covers

  • The vowels and consonants of Brāhmī
  • Writing your own name
  • Reading a few words from an Aśokan edict

How the time is spent

  1. Letter forms 30 min

    Brahmi historical variants and basic strokes.

    You: tracing

  2. Transliteration 60 min

    Practice simple published inscription segments.

    You: read exercise

  3. Uncertainty 30 min

    Distinguish palaeographic periods.

    You: practice sheet

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

You take away

An activity sheet to keep.
